persona.bio: Beauty advisor at a department store makeup counter, paid partly on commission. Makeovers and color matching, restocking testers, cleaning the counter, keeping her client book, texting her clients when new launches come in or there's a gift with purchase, hitting her sales goals, events on weekends. Texting clients and keeping the client book take the most time outside makeovers. She texts clients from her own iPhone. She tried an AI app once and didn't trust it. Her store restricts AI.

steps.firstStep: I’m a beauty advisor at a department store makeup counter, and I send follow up texts to clients after a visit or when a new product arrives. Write a short, friendly text, two or three sentences, that sounds warm and personal, not pushy. Keep it casual, the way I’d text a regular client. Here is what this one is about: [paste what the text is for, like a new product, a restock or a visit follow up].

steps.note: I work as a beauty advisor at a department store makeup counter, and part of my pay is commission. I write to clients by text, mostly to follow up after a visit or answer a quick question. My tone is warm, friendly and upbeat, never pushy. I like short messages, one to three sentences, that sound like me. Never add details I did not give you, like prices, shade names, stock or dates. Use square brackets for anything I need to fill in. Never invent offers. Give me the draft only, and I will read it and change it before I send it.

steps.title: Your follow up texts, saved once on your phone
steps.read: Your follow up texts live on your phone’s keyboard, each a few letters away. You stop starting from a blank message many times a day. Each reply still sounds like you, and you change only the small details before you send it.

safeUse: Never type a client’s full name, phone number, address or email into a chat tool.
Never type skin conditions, allergies or other health details a client told you.
Never paste your client book or any notes about a client into a chat tool.
Check with your company before using any AI tool for work, since yours is restricted.
Read every text before it goes out, and fill in the square brackets yourself.
Never type prices, stock levels or sales numbers that are not public.
steps.askMessage: Hi [manager’s name], I’d like to know which AI tools are approved for my work at the counter and what I may use them for. I have two tasks in mind: writing follow up texts to clients and answering client messages. I would only put in general wording, never client names or private details, and I would read everything before it goes out. I’d also like to know whether I may use AI to help keep my client book up to date, since I know that may need approval first. Could you let me know, or point me to the right person in IT?

design.today: You write these many times a day, each one from scratch. You work from your phone, and your last one was a short text about the new bronze palette and a lip gloss set aside.
design.newWay: Your company restricts AI for work, so AI does not touch these texts or any client details. Instead you build a small set of your own follow up texts, written by you in your own voice, and keep them where you can reach them fast on your phone. Each day you pick the one that fits, add the client's name and the product, and send it yourself. That keeps your tone personal and spares you starting from a blank screen.

steps.goal: List the few kinds of follow up you send most, such as a new arrival, a thank you after a makeover, or a restock of a favorite.
Write one short text for each kind in your own words, with a gap where the name and product go.
Keep the finished texts in one place on your phone that your company allows, so each is quick to find.
Read through the set once a season and swap in new products and offers.

material.label: Follow up text set
material.what: Your own short texts for each kind of follow up, with gaps for the client's name and the product.

material.label: Tone notes
material.what: A few lines on how you sound with clients, so every text still reads like you.

design.checkPoint: You fill in each gap and read the text before you send it yourself.

design.today: Client messages come in all day and each needs a quick reply. Much of it happens in text messages on your phone.
design.newWay: Because AI is restricted at your company, no AI reads or answers client messages. You set up your own list of replies to the questions you hear most, such as what is in stock, what time you are in, and how to book. When a message comes in, you pick the matching reply, adjust a line for that client and send it. Answers stay consistent and quick, and you stay in control of every word.

steps.goal: Pick the ten questions clients ask you most often.
Write a short, friendly answer to each one in your own words.
Save the answers on your phone in a way your company allows, so each one is a few taps away.
Add a new answer whenever the same question comes up a third time.

material.label: Top ten replies
material.what: Your own written answers to the ten questions clients ask most.

material.label: Booking reply
material.what: A short message with your hours and how a client can book a visit.

design.checkPoint: You read each reply and change anything that does not fit that client before you send it yourself.
